sources.title: Dún an Óir: the 1580 siege and massacre
sources.annotation: Irish heritage site identifies approx. 600 surrendered people killed, including women and children; modern monument not equal 1580 siege geometry

sources.title: Revisiting Smerwick: Spenser and Massacre (Jane Grogan, 2023 event)
sources.annotation: Describes Grey contemporary report alleging 600 slain, acknowledges divergent accounts; do not double count

sources.title: An Italian account of the siege and massacre at Smerwick (Aoibheann Mullan, 2007)
sources.annotation: 13 pp article Journal Kerry Archaeological Historical Society 7:2 pp70–82; original Italian account requires reading

sources.title: Annals of the Four Masters, vol 1580 section M1580.26
sources.annotation: John Burke retook Loughrea from English constable Master Jones in 1580. Seventeenth-century compilation, not contemporary garrison register

sources.title: The Desmond Survey, introduction & manuscript calendared extracts
sources.annotation: Forfeiture surveys 1584–86, 1586 Munster seignories, 1587 Francis Jobson Limerick map, 1589 Munster map; original surveys partly destroyed in 1922

sources.issuer: Digital Repository of Ireland / Trinity College Dublin
sources.title: Francis Jobson, The Province of Munster (30 May 1589)
sources.annotation: Map inscribed to Burghley, c. 8 English miles per inch; land tenures from survey; digital image/usage terms require separate review

sources.title: Francis Jobson 1589 Munster map photostat MS 16 L 10 (38); TCD MS 1209 (36)
sources.annotation: Independent original/copy shelfmarks of 1589 Munster map; no coordinates extracted

sources.title: Decolonial Deep Mapping (map analyses of 1586 and 1589 Munster plantations)
sources.annotation: 1586 map depicts sought allocations; 1589 Jobson marked named undertakers and estate lines; do not call planned allotments occupied

sources.issuer: Archivo Histórico de la Nobleza, Ministerio de Cultura (Spain)
sources.title: Felipe II orders Álvaro de Bazán to pursue Drake, 18 May 1586, SANTA CRUZ C48 D7 f20
sources.annotation: Philip II explicitly references Drake robbing and ransoming Santo Domingo; a Spanish adverse-party official attestation, NOT English net-revenue account

sources.issuer: Archivo General de la Nación, Dominican Republic
sources.title: Saqueo e incendio de Santo Domingo por Francis Drake, 1586-04-17
sources.review_status: Catalogue read, report body not examined
sources.annotation: AGI Santo Domingo legajo 14 transcription reference, contemporaneous report on plunder and fire

sources.issuer: Museo Histórico de Cartagena de Indias
sources.title: Plano del Asalto de Drake a Cartagena de Indias / 1586
sources.annotation: 110,000 ducats reported for ransom, 6-week occupation, urban destruction; 1599 de Bry image postdates campaign and not true surveyed wall polygon

sources.title: Drake's Great Armada, 1586 Cartagena ransom account
sources.annotation: English participants' account states 110,000 ducats, and notes a further 1,000 crowns for priory. Do not treat different units as net royal receipts

sources.title: Fort Raleigh: 1585 The Military Colony
sources.annotation: English military colony, Wingina/Pemisapan killed by Ralph Lane in 1586; fort & native polity distinction

sources.title: Fort Raleigh: 1587 The Lost Colony
sources.annotation: English colonists mistakenly attacked allied Croatoan community; violence neither Spanish sea loot nor English slave commerce

sources.title: Fort Raleigh official brochure on initial privateering base
sources.annotation: 1585 military/privateering base purpose and 1587 settlement failure; never fill whole modern NC as colony

sources.title: Timeline of transatlantic slave trade and abolition
sources.annotation: Explicit Hawkins trafficking 1562–69 and first established English enterprise 1618; cannot invent new 1580s slaving voyages from this overview

sources.title: Britain and the Transatlantic Slave Trade
sources.annotation: John Lok 1555, Towerson 1556–57, Hawkins 1562 onward; distinguish chapter 8/9 history from new 1580s journeys

sources.issuer: National Library of Ireland / UCC CELT
sources.title: A Briefe description of Ireland made in 1589, by Robert Payne (printed edition commentary)
sources.review_status: Read introduction, number not verified original rent roll
sources.annotation: Editor cites 574,628 acres escheated after 1586 act, derived from later printed historical commentary; not area actually settled or income

sources.title: The Capture of the Santa Ana, Cabo San Lucas, November 1587 (Mathes 1969)
sources.annotation: 1969 edition reproduces both English Francis Pretty and Spanish Antonio de Sierra/Tomás de Alzola statements; values and dates await source cross-check

sources.issuer: Royal Spanish regional heritage department (Junta de Andalucía)
sources.title: 1587 Drake Cádiz attack: wreck San Giorgio e Sant’Elmo Buonaventura archaeological identification
sources.annotation: 1587 attacked Genoese merchant ship in Cádiz bay, archaeological wreck Delta II; wreck location not precise without official GIS

sources.title: Desmond Survey, 1586-89 geographic estate and rent entries
sources.annotation: Original Latin documents burned 1922, only surviving calendars and extracts; source map map scale not sufficient for direct modern georeferencing

sources.title: Thomas Cavendish's visit to Puná Island in 1587
sources.review_status: Article located; details await extended read
sources.annotation: Site for Cavendish Pacific raid. Puná island geography does not indicate English sovereignty

editorial_note: Only claims directly supported by cited sources can pass Atlas review; URLs/catalogue references and unread manuscripts do not establish primary text contents.
